traits.division_planes.note: FEIS's common yarrow review (Aleksoff 1999, read 2026-10-17), after Gleason and Cronquist: the native forms' narrow leaf segments stand in several planes, so the leaf is three-dimensional, where the European form's lie flat. iNaturalist photos of Pacific Northwest plants agree. It is the segments that stand so: the primary divisions keep two ranks, so the leaf is a feathery strap, oblong or lanceolate in outline as leaf_shape says, as the 28 imagekit photos show it, not a bottlebrush round its rachis.

traits.height_typical_m.note: FEIS's common yarrow review (Aleksoff 1999, read 2026-10-15): a perennial forb 11 to 40 inches (30-100 cm) in height with extensive rhizomes.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an aromatic herb with feathery, finely divided leaves and flat-topped clusters of small white flowers. Not fitted to measurements. leaf_area (0.048) and basal_area (0.032) are the shares of a 1 m card the stem and basal leaves draw (species test `builtin_species_shade_with_the_area_they_draw`), raised on 2026-11-07 when the leaves were drawn wider and their lobes fuller.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.55 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: soft grey-green leaves; white flower clusters.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its flat-topped array drawn head by head (spec rework L1c): its kind, its primary branches, how many heads it bears, its level top and how densely the heads crowd come from its characters, by the rules at the flowering plants, and each head's size and rays from its involucre and ray florets, by the daisy family's rules (2026-11-06; before, each head was set by hand at 6 mm on pedicels leaning 40 degrees, which drew a cone of bare stalks). Broad rays round a disc half the head's width, and the bare stalk below the array's lowest branches, by eye.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: FNA's account of the species: plants 6 to 65 cm tall or more; blades oblong or lanceolate, once or twice pinnately lobed; 10 to over 100 heads in flat-topped, corymb-like arrays; 20 to 30 phyllaries in about three rows; rays 5 to 8 (as few as 3); 10 to 20 disc florets; fruits 1 to 2 mm.

traits.receptacle_shape.note: FNA's account of the species, as search results quote copies of its text (the pages themselves were not read): receptacles convex, their paleae lanceolate, 1.5 to 4 mm.

traits.leaf_incision.note: VicFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): leaves 1- or 2-pinnatisect, cut to the midrib, the ultimate lobes spreading in more than one plane. FNA's 'once or twice pinnately lobed, the ultimate lobes lanceolate, often in several planes' describes the same blade; 'dissected' is the vocabulary's word for one cut into fine segments.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The blade drawn dissected (spec rework P4): a twice-divided leaf whose segments run together along a winged rachis, its pattern and the running together from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, separate toothed leaflets stood along a rachis. Counts and form by eye from iNaturalist photographs (2026-10-17): a narrow strap of many short primary segments set close, about one segment's width apart, 30 pairs on a stem leaf and 40 on a basal one, at about 60 degrees to the rachis, each cut into about 7 short lobes, each about a third as wide as long, spreading about 60 degrees from the segment's own rachis so the lobes fan out and the leaf reads as a feathery strap (2026-11-07, re-read against iNaturalist observations 758272, 126222917, 196397969, 391805083 and 488340760: at 45 degrees the lobes lay along their segment and the leaf drew as a wire with ticks beside every photo; lobes half as wide as long filled the blade so far that the card tiers baked the leaves into the plant's cards as dots); the segments longest 0.4 of the way up and shorter toward both ends, the blade's oblong to lanceolate outline (its shape word is the blade's, so the card sets its segments' own form by hand).

appearance.organs.basal.shape.note: The blade drawn dissected (spec rework P4): a twice-divided leaf whose segments run together along a winged rachis, its pattern and the running together from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, separate toothed leaflets stood along a rachis. Counts and form by eye from iNaturalist photographs (2026-10-17): a narrow strap of many short primary segments set close, about one segment's width apart, 30 pairs on a stem leaf and 40 on a basal one, at about 60 degrees to the rachis, each cut into about 7 short lobes, each about a third as wide as long, spreading about 60 degrees from the segment's own rachis so the lobes fan out and the leaf reads as a feathery strap (2026-11-07, re-read against iNaturalist observations 758272, 126222917, 196397969, 391805083 and 488340760: at 45 degrees the lobes lay along their segment and the leaf drew as a wire with ticks beside every photo; lobes half as wide as long filled the blade so far that the card tiers baked the leaves into the plant's cards as dots); the segments longest 0.4 of the way up and shorter toward both ends, the blade's oblong to lanceolate outline (its shape word is the blade's, so the card sets its segments' own form by hand).

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured from iNaturalist photos where the leaves fill the frame (2026-11-07; observations 391805083, 126222917 and 488340760; plantgen-claude project-files/library-api/yarrow-2026-11-07/): the median green pixel's linear red is 0.6 of its green and its blue 0.24, yellower than the herb green the plant was drawn in (0.47, 0.33). Photos are exposed brighter than leaves are, so only the hue comes from them; the green channel is a basal-leaf green as other forbs state it (sRGB 120). The stems take it as a herb's do, where they were drawn pale yellow-grey beside near-black leaves.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Measured by eye from iNaturalist photos: in 2026-10-17 a leaf about 10 cm long held against a hand (observation 758272) was a strap 1.2 to 1.5 cm wide, about 7 times as long as wide; on 2026-11-07 the flat-lying basal and stem leaves of observations 126222917, 196397969, 391805083 and 488340760 are 5 to 6 times as long as wide, so the range runs from the shortest leaves, 5 cm long at about 6 times as long as wide, to 20 cm ones at about 6 (0.008 to 0.035 m). Abrams and Ferris give lengths only.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, varieties of A. millefolium (pp. 390-391): leaves mostly 5-20 cm long; 10-30 cm in var. californica and 15-40 cm in var. gigantea.

traits.ray_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. millefolium (p. 390): the 3-8 broad rays are generally white, now and then pink. Word: white.

traits.disc_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. millefolium (p. 390): disc florets the same colour as the rays, i.e. white (an off-white given). Word: white (same as rays).

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, varieties of A. millefolium (pp. 390-391): heads/involucres mostly 4-7 mm high, up to 9 mm in var. californica.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, varieties of A. millefolium (pp. 390-391): flowering periods given per variety run from March (vars. californica, arenicola) to November (var. arenicola); most varieties May to August.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's common yarrow review (Aleksoff 1999, read 2026-10-16), table of average dates at five elevations in Utah (Ephraim Canyon): "seeds ripe" from August 26 to September 28; read as August and September. It gives no Pacific Northwest dates.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. millefolium (pp. 390-391): plants rhizomatous to tufted; rhizomes short and stout in some varieties, long and slender in others.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2908230), as no source read gives it.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2908230), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of China, Achillea millefolium (read 2026-10-18): the ultimate leaf segments end in a tiny hard (cartilaginous) point.

traits.inflorescence_outline.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, A. millefolium (p. 390): heads numerous, aggregated into flat to round-topped, corymbiform panicles; FNA's arrays are flat-topped (see traits). Word: flat_topped.

traits.inflorescence_density.note: VicFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read, 2026-11-06): capitula in dense compound corymbs. The 28 iNaturalist photographs of yarrow in imagekit (batches pilot-asteraceae-2026-10-31 and inat-lowpoly-r8-2026-10-29) agree: one plate of heads with no gaps between its branches. Word: dense.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: Counted by eye from the 28 iNaturalist photographs of yarrow in imagekit (batches pilot-asteraceae-2026-10-31 and inat-lowpoly-r8-2026-10-29) (2026-11-06): each plate is made of about 5 to 12 rounded tufts of heads, one on each primary branch of the compound array Abrams and Ferris (p. 390, 'corymbiform panicles') and VicFlora ('dense compound corymbs') describe. No flora read counts them.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: FNA's account of the genus Achillea (Trock), as SEINet's copy is quoted in search results (the page itself was not read, 2026-11-06): involucres campanulate to hemispheric, mostly 2-3(-5+) mm diam.

traits.ray_length_m.note: FNA's account of the species, as SEINet's copy is quoted in search results (the page itself was not read, 2026-11-06): ray florets (3-)5-8, laminae 1.5-3 x 1.5-3 mm. Abrams and Ferris (p. 390): rays broadly ovate to orbicular.

traits.ray_width_m.note: FNA's account of the species, as SEINet's copy is quoted in search results (the page itself was not read, 2026-11-06): ray florets (3-)5-8, laminae 1.5-3 x 1.5-3 mm. Abrams and Ferris (p. 390): rays broadly ovate to orbicular.
